title: Intent-Based Infrastructure and Service Orchestration Using Agentic-AI
V95_REASON: Implemented agentic intent-based network/infrastructure orchestration translates natural-language intent into IaC-backed Kubernetes/service provisioning and evaluates real task completion. Published implementation emphasizes graph-state controlled execution and configuration quality, but does not establish a separate premise/authority/validity recheck immediately before deployment commit.

title: Demonstrating Multi-Agent Collaboration via Agent-to-Agent and Model Context Protocols: An IT Incident Response Case Study
V95_REASON: A2A+MCP reference implementation coordinates agents for IT incident response and evaluates automated remediation using simulated incidents. It demonstrates collaboration and remediation quality, not a validated production action-admission/revalidation gate.
V95_EVIDENCE_SOURCE: IEEE SOSE/CISOSE official paper page, DOI 10.1109/SOSE67019.2025.00013

title: Operational Intelligence for Incident Management through OSS MCP-Based Agentic Orchestration
V95_REASON: Prototype orchestrates Datadog, PagerDuty and Slack through MCP to assemble diagnostic evidence and generate a structured first investigation update after incident assignment. The demonstrated endpoint is investigation support, not consequential remediation commit.

title: Intelligent Multi-Agent Orchestration Framework for Enterprise Financial Systems
V95_REASON: Enterprise financial multi-agent framework routes requests to transaction, risk, compliance and advisory agents using deterministic/LLM routing plus confidence-based fallback. Evidence supports routing quality and reduced manual handling, but not explicit validation/authorization of a pending financial transaction before effect.

title: AI-Enhanced Management and Control (MC) Architecture for Multi-Layer and Multi-Domain Optical Networks
V95_REASON: Optical-network management/control architecture uses A2A for cross-domain orchestration and MCP for standardized tool invocation. Available evidence establishes orchestration/interoperability, not a demonstrated pre-commit validity gate for network configuration changes.

title: A Semantic-Consistent Privacy Middleware for MCP-driven Penetration Testing
V95_REASON: MCP Privacy Middleware is a local-trust-boundary bidirectional proxy that sanitizes dynamic tool-generated context before exposure to remote LLM services. It is a concrete privacy-control boundary, but protects confidentiality rather than revalidating the correctness/authority of a consequential agent decision before external effect.

title: Model context protocol for MBSE: a unified interoperable agentic framework for systems modelling
V95_REASON: Open-access MCP-for-SysML-v2 framework enables LLM agents to interact with system models through standardized APIs and demonstrates automated modelling interoperability. It provides agentic MBSE infrastructure, not consequential action validity enforcement.
V95_EVIDENCE_SOURCE: Cambridge Proceedings of the Design Society full text, DOI 10.1017/pds.2026.10630

title: Protocol-Driven Multi-Agent Orchestration for Federated Distributed Analytics
V95_REASON: Agentic Router Architecture explicitly models routing as constrained optimization balancing accuracy, latency, governance and cost, with a protocol for trust negotiation and execution coordination. This is directly relevant to governed execution, but accessible evidence is architectural/complexity-level and does not demonstrate a per-action runtime commit gate in a consequential deployment.

title: CoMAS-HPC: A Collaborative Multi-Agent System for HPC Administration
V95_REASON: CoMAS-HPC autonomously manages HPC administrative domains and demonstrates coordinated intervention in a thermal crisis, resolving it within five minutes while preventing hardware damage. This is consequential autonomous operation, but the source does not identify a distinct state/premise/authority validation step governing intervention before effect.

title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning-Based Event-Driven Scheduling for Multi-UAV Periodic Inspection
V95_REASON: Paper is a multi-agent reinforcement-learning scheduling method for periodic multi-UAV inspection. Source evidence places it in conventional MARL scheduling/optimization rather than LLM/agentic tool-execution governance or a validity-preserving commit boundary.

title: Preventing Wrong Work Item Retrieval in LLM-Based MCP Systems Through Multi-Agent Validation
V95_REASON: The paper explicitly introduces multi-agent validation to prevent wrong work-item retrieval in LLM-based MCP systems and is framed as improving reliability by validating retrieved results. This is a direct decision-validity mechanism, but accessible source evidence is insufficient to establish whether validation controls a consequential external commit rather than only retrieval correctness.
V95_EVIDENCE_SOURCE: AICCONF 2026 official accepted-paper/program evidence + author summary, DOI 10.1109/AICCONF69182.2026.11600651
